story.title: The Last Echo
story.logline: A man discovers his smart home assistant has been recording the future instead of the past.
story.theme: The terrifying inevitability of pre-recorded reality.
story.twist: The assistant was not predicting tomorrow, but playing back the exact moment of his death.
story.ending: A final haunting question about whether we can ever change a fate that has already been spoken.

scenes.narration: My smart speaker just told me to cancel tonight's flight, using a voice I have never heard before.
scenes.visual_prompt: Close-up of Leo, a 28-year-old man with messy brown hair and a gray hoodie, staring at a glowing smart speaker in a dark minimalist apartment.
scenes.camera: Extreme close-up pushing in rapidly on the blinking blue light.

scenes.narration: Leo, twenty-eight, in the same gray hoodie, touches the speaker, demanding to know who spoke inside his locked apartment.
scenes.visual_prompt: Medium shot of Leo, 28-year-old man with messy brown hair in a gray hoodie, reaching out nervously toward the glowing speaker in his dark apartment.
scenes.camera: Eye-level tracking shot following his hand.

scenes.narration: The device does not answer with silence. It plays back the sound of my own panic from tomorrow morning.
scenes.visual_prompt: Medium close-up of Leo, 28-year-old man with messy brown hair and a gray hoodie, listening intently with wide, terrified eyes in his dark apartment.
scenes.camera: Static low-angle shot focusing on his trembling jaw.

scenes.narration: Leo, wearing his gray hoodie, paces across the wooden floorboards, realizing the timestamp on the file reads four hours ahead.
scenes.visual_prompt: Wide shot of Leo, 28-year-old man with messy brown hair in a gray hoodie, pacing frantically across the dimly lit wooden floor of his apartment.
scenes.camera: Whip pan following his desperate movement.

scenes.narration: I try to unplug the machine, but the cord vanishes into my own hand like smoke in the wind.
scenes.visual_prompt: Close-up of Leo, 28-year-old man with messy brown hair in a gray hoodie, grabbing at a disappearing black cord inside his dark apartment.
scenes.camera: Handheld macro shot focusing on his fingers passing through solid plastic.

scenes.narration: Leo, still trapped in the gray hoodie, hears the front door handle jiggle violently as someone tries to break in.
scenes.visual_prompt: Medium shot of Leo, 28-year-old man with messy brown hair in a gray hoodie, spinning around to face the front door of his dark apartment.
scenes.camera: Over-the-shoulder shot framing the shaking doorknob.

scenes.narration: The speaker whispers my exact final words, begging for mercy against an intruder who looks just like me.
scenes.visual_prompt: Medium close-up of Leo, 28-year-old man with messy brown hair in a gray hoodie, mouthing words in sync with the glowing speaker in his dark apartment.
scenes.camera: Push-in shot locking onto his terrified lips.

scenes.narration: Leo, holding his breath in the gray hoodie, sees the lock snap open and the darkness flood inside the room.
scenes.visual_prompt: Wide shot of Leo, 28-year-old man with messy brown hair in a gray hoodie, backing away as shadows pour through the front door of his apartment.
scenes.camera: Slow pull-back revealing the shrinking space around him.

scenes.narration: The terrifying truth hits me: the past can be changed, but the future has already buried us.
scenes.visual_prompt: Close-up of Leo, 28-year-old man with messy brown hair in a gray hoodie, shedding a single tear illuminated by the speaker in his dark apartment.
scenes.camera: Slow motion close-up tracking the tear.

scenes.narration: If your final words were already recorded right now, would you still bother saying anything at all?
scenes.visual_prompt: Extreme close-up of the dead, dark speaker sitting alone on the wooden table inside the empty apartment of Leo, 28-year-old man.
scenes.camera: Static locked-off shot holding in total darkness.

caption.title: The Last Echo
caption.caption:
Alex thought his smart speaker was glitching when it replayed tomorrow's noises. But tonight, it played the sound of his own front door kicking in.

Can you ever really outrun a destiny that's already been filed away?
